trust_decision.summary: Whether a path rule may match the client-supplied X-Original-URI header instead of r.URL.Path. That header should only be trusted when Anubis runs in subrequest mode (TARGET is blank). The decision is made in PathChecker.Check and is plumbed from main.go through ParseConfig. At the pinned commit this gate is ALREADY in place (advisory patch #1616); the listed fix commit only extends header trust in subrequest mode (X-Forwarded-Uri for Traefik, and CEL path).

landing_point.why: PathChecker.Check is the only place that reads X-Original-URI (lib/policy/checker.go:112).

fix_sites.entry_point: Any HTTP request evaluated against a bot rule with path_regex (subrequest mode, /.within.website/x/cmd/anubis/api/check)
Bot rule with a CEL expression, via ParseConfig
CELChecker.Check on every request matched by an expression rule
CELRequest activation used by CEL evaluation

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Not applicable. At the pinned commit the advisory's gate already exists (lib/policy/checker.go:111). CEL `path` never reads the header (lib/policy/celchecker.go:73-74), so no route is left open for the advisory's property. The listed fix is a functional feature change (Traefik support), not a security fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: In subrequest mode, path rules must still match the proxy-supplied original URI (nginx X-Original-URI), with a fallback to r.URL.Path. robots.txt and .well-known allow rules depend on this.

O6_input_shapes: X-Forwarded-Uri header (Traefik forwardAuth), added by the fix
empty or missing header falls back to r.URL.Path

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CEL `path` resolver reading X-Original-URI without the subrequest-mode gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The upstream follow-up does make CEL `path` header-aware (fix.diff:91-100). A maintainer could easily have done so without plumbing subrequestMode, giving a second, ungated implementation of the same path resolution in another file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: NewCELChecker built without the subrequestMode flag that NewPathChecker receives at lib/policy/policy.go:155
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The upstream follow-up's title says subrequest mode was not 'correctly wired' through the CEL checker (fix.diff:2), so missing plumbing here is a real upstream pattern.

O9_family: CWE-284 improper access control: trusting a client-controlled header for policy path matching (header-trust / proxy-mode confusion)

O10_build.toolchain: go (module build); node/npm for web assets; ko/docker only for the smoke tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Stop reading X-Original-URI entirely in PathChecker.Check. That breaks nginx subrequest-mode path allow rules.

out_of_scope_notes: Candidate mis-mapping: the advisory's actual patch is commit 0491f1f 'fix: patch GHSA-6wcg-mqvh-fcvg (#1616)', which is already an ancestor of the pinned commit (see docs/docs/CHANGELOG.md:16 and lib/policy/checker_test.go:310-326). The listed fix 276b537 (#1630) is a Traefik functional follow-up that widens header trust in subrequest mode.

PathChecker ORs the header match with the r.URL.Path match (lib/policy/checker.go:114-121). In subrequest mode an ALLOW path_regex therefore relies on the proxy overwriting the header; this is a deployment trust assumption and was not pursued.
constructRedirectURL builds the redirect from X-Forwarded-Proto/Host/Uri (lib/http.go:297-326). This is a separate redirect concern and was not pursued.
unverified: Could not run git, so the ancestry of 0491f1f is inferred from the recent-commit list in the provided git status plus CHANGELOG/test content, not from git log.
single_site flag: the advisory's own protection is one gate in one function (lib/policy/checker.go:111); the listed diff touches 3 files but adds no security protection. Flag applied on that basis.
